items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: I would put on that Dave Koz and I had my little transcription book and I would just close my eyes and play.

ctx.x: Him and then even more I think my first two saxophone CDs I was given was Kenny G and Dave Koz, so another smooth jazz guy. And I remember, and like I said, I grew up with pop. This was basically pop so this made sense to me, but it was done by a saxophone. It was done by the instrument that I’m playing. And it sounded really good to me. And I’m really grateful for those first two CDs because it was that music that got me to kind of, I think, break outside of the box in the way of like kind of taking it as my own…

wanted to like, hey are there transcription books with this? I want to play along with this. And then I remember taking the CD and this little boom box that I had and I would go out to the garage, and this was in Michigan and in the winter it would get really cold in the garage, but it didn’t matter, I would go in that garage because it had the best acoustics in the house, you know this nice reverb. And I would put on that Dave Koz and I had my little transcription book and I would just close my eyes and play.…
Very significant. I did the same thing with Cannonball Adderley. Talking about filling the horn.
